💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 14:15.
  • Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund but appears to have avoided a serious injury, Mikel Arteta has unveiled.
  • The Spain international collided with Newcastle United striker Will Osula in the second half of Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw and had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 14:15.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund but appears to have avoided a serious injury, Mikel Arteta has unveiled.

The Spain international collided with Newcastle United striker Will Osula in the second half of Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw and had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya was in visible pain as an Arsenal physio supported his arm and shoulder, and Arteta admitted at full time that his number one having to come off was "not good news".

The Arsenal boss also revealed that Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to assess the seriousness of the issue, and on the same day, he was photographed with his arm in a sling in London.

@TouchlineX Raya yesterday in Oxford Circus... https://t.co/6NVmuNDLzZ.

However, speaking to reporters in his pre-game press conference, Arteta delivered a reassuring update on Raya, who has seemingly avoided a fracture or dislocation and will not need to go under the knife.

In a recent development, "He’s not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected," Arteta told the media.

Sources indicate that "We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test we have done shows something that is much more encouraging. There is no need for surgery. Tomorrow we will have more tests and we will know [more].".

Arteta did not directly rule Raya out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester City either, potentially handing Arsenal a monumental boost ahead of the visit of Enzo Maresca's side.

The 31-year-old has already kept 10 clean sheets in 16 appearances for the Gunners this season, and he is also believed to have agreed a upcoming long-term contract with Arsenal; his current deal expires in 2028.

Raya has only missed one Arsenal game through injury since originally joining on loan from Brentford in January 2023 - the 5-1 EFL Cup third-round win over Bolton Wanderers in September 2024.

With Raya sidelined, Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to make just his second Champions League start for Arsenal on Tuesday, after appearing in January's 3-2 victory over Kairat Almaty.

However, Arteta could throw a curveball and select Illan Meslier, whose first and only appearance for the Gunners so far came in their horrendous EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

The Frenchman has also never played in the Champions League in his career, while Kepa has appeared in the competition 22 times and was Chelsea's starting goalkeeper during their run to the 2022-23 quarter-finals.

As the latter has also held his position as Arteta's number two despite Meslier's arrival, there should be no doubt over Arsenal's starting goalkeeper against Borussia Dortmund.

Hot on the heels of the launch of the Scottish government’s ‘Project 2035’ drive to make Scotland a leading force in women’s football comes the news that Scotland will host Women’s World Cup games during that same year.

Sources indicate that the tournament, to be jointly staged with England, Northern Ireland and Wales, will see games played at Hampden Park and Easter Road in Edinburgh. So girls dreaming of footballing glory can now add the spine-tingling Hampden roar to imagined wondergoals.

According to recent reports, the gap between such reveries and reality usually requires a considerable amount of hard work to bridge. However, in order to achieve a dream, one first needs to have it.

If large numbers of girls take up the sport, it will not only benefit the Scottish national side, but society as a whole. Everyone, no matter their age or gender, should be physically active – humans are simply not designed to exist in the seated position.

If we embrace the idea of being a ‘sporting nation’, we will be both happier and healthier. And that, as much as World Cup glory, is a dream we should all share.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roy Keane remarked Brighton’s “sloppy” finishing cost them dearly but gave all the credit to Hull City's determination after they stunned the Seagulls with two late goals to claim a 2-0 Premier League victory.

The Seagulls looked the better side for much of Sunday's contest, creating numerous opportunities but failing to find a way past an inspired Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Brighton were made to pay for their wastefulness when Oli McBurnie struck twice in stoppage time, following Costinha's late dismissal for a second yellow card.

And former Manchester United captain Keane believes Hull deserve enormous credit for their fighting spirit after sustained pressure from Albion.

"It's a mad game. The sending off had a major impact. Brighton were desperately trying to win the game, and you have to give credit to them, but they left spaces and gaps," Keane told Sky Sports.

It has been revealed that "It's brilliant from Hull, great fighting spirit and a bit of quality. Great composure from McBurnie. You think McBurnie has missed the opportunity, but what a huge goal.".

Keane was also keen to highlight the contribution of Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis, who produced a string of outstanding saves to frustrate Fabian Hurzeler's side.

"Instead of being critical of Brighton, you have to give credit to the goalkeeper," he added.

"They might not have Brighton's quality, but they demonstrated great fighting spirit, composure, and stayed in the game; you have to give them huge credit for that.".

The result leaves Brighton second in the Premier League table with 22 points from 11 matches, while Hull climb to 11th with 14 points.

Albion will look to respond when they welcome Newcastle United to the Amex Stadium on Sunday, November 29 (2.05pm).

Hull, meanwhile, travel to Crystal Palace on the same afternoon as they look to build on an impressive victory.

Breaking: Celtic boss Martin O’Neill problems big Kieran Tierney patch as fitness levels and position assessed

  • Although the Celtic manager substituted Tierney towards the end of Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren, the player started – and finished – both of Scotland’s games in the recent international window, when he was deployed as left centre-half in a back-three formation favoured by newly introduced international manager Sebastien Pocognoli.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Martin O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is back to his very best and harbours no fears about the defender’s fitness levels ahead of a frantic festive schedule.

Although the Celtic manager substituted Tierney towards the end of Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren, the player started – and finished – both of Scotland’s games in the recent international window, when he was deployed as left centre-half in a back-three formation favoured by newly introduced international manager Sebastien Pocognoli.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

O’Neill admits this could be an option for Celtic if he chooses to play a system that he once was synonymous with during his first spell in charge at the club.

“Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it,” mentioned O’Neill. “He competes better in the air than I ever thought he did.

“It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that. He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.”.

Celtic face a tough upcoming run of games, including travelling to take on second-tier Portuguese club Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night. Two more away games against Hearts and Dundee quickly follow. The Parkhead side have just one more home match – against St Johnstone – before Christmas. Two other assignments, against Aberdeen and Omonia Nicosia, are away.

O’Neill has already spoken of “manoeuvring” players in the first-team squad to ensure no one is pushed beyond their limits.

Tierney clearly merits the most concern given his injury history. However, he has been quietly putting in the minutes for his club as well as his country in recent weeks. He has played the full 90 minutes of two of Celtic’s last four matches and was only subbed off on Saturday with 20 minutes left against St Mirren with the game already won. O’Neill revealed that he has a crafty tactic for dealing with the player if he begins to look like he might want to come off; he pretends not to notice him. There is no point in the player looking forlornly towards the dugout.

“Tierney played two 90 minutes for Scotland and that made it difficult for him to last the full game against St Mirren,” said O'Neill.

It has been revealed that “Internationals take it out of you and he played every second. He played left centre back and that maybe means less running, but those games are tough.

In a recent development, “Previous to his injury, he was feeling it. But since he’s been back, he’s played a lot of games. Sometimes with Kieran, when you feel as if he’s flagging, you just ignore him. If he’s coming near you, you turn away because you want him to play the games!

“Kieran has done great for me,” he added. "He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too. Kieran will be major for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

“Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal. He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too.

Industry observers note that “I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about Kieran. He’s a great lad too - very popular in the dressing room.”.

Alfred Johansson insists Motherwell’s latest accounts show the club are trending upwards - with Norway’s Bodo Glimt a key reference point.

It has been revealed that the Premiership side have reported a profit of £2.3M, which rises to £3.1M when excluding depreciation and finance costs, for the 2025/26 financial year. A record of £5M was generated from player trading while former manager Jens Berthel Askou achieved a fourth place finish in last term’s top flight.

Current manager Johansson’s work was largely in Scandinavia before travelling to Motherwell. He watched Bodo’s rise from lowly divisions to Champions League competitors and feels that demonstrates what a step-by-step approach can do for a club’s long term aspirations. Former Rosenborg gaffer Johansson mentioned: “I can't really use that to ask for more time in terms of performing but definitely, it's evidence of what the club has been doing for the past 18 months at least, that it’s something that is working.

Industry observers note that “So that alignment in the club, that philosophy, and that strategy, like we do things like this, and the connection I feel between people inside here and the offices, that everyone wants to pull together in that direction. That is what gives you output all the time.

Sources indicate that “This is a club that the budget is very small compared with some of the teams that we want to compete with. That was the same for Bodo/Glimt 10 years ago. Their budget was so small, they went down to the 2nd division in Norway, now they are playing Champions League. You have to build stone by stone, and that's what Motherwell are trying to do, and that's what I feel every day inside these walls.”.

In a recent development, motherwell’s long-term goals are also set to be boosted by a training base being built at nearby Dalziel Park where they currently undergo preparation for matches. Johansson is keen to see the club build on its ability to grasp marginal gains. He explained: ”You don't have that much time in football nowadays. I get asked in the press conference about patience and everything is related to time.

It has been revealed that “That means that you have to make the most out of your time. Maybe before 30 years ago you had to optimise every week. Now you have to optimise every hour in top football. That's down to recovery of players, work with their bodies, and you need facilities to be able to facilitate that work. So that's one part of it.

“That you need to add the facilities for the players to be able to do the work that's needed to play every few days and with that intensity that. Now I saw that from all the top leagues in Europe, that the Scottish Premiership was the second in the world in explosive accelerations, for instance.

In a recent development, “That's one of the more demanding things that you can put the body through. So you need to be able to react. You need to recover from that between matches and trainings, and so on. So you need the facilities for that. We don't have that much time. Right now we are driving back and forth to Dalziel Park. I could maybe take five minutes in my office with a player or on the pitch talking to a player. All of this is optimising time and I think it's essential today.”.

Industry observers note that dundee boss Steven Pressley spoke last week of the lack of national performance centre in Scotland, like Sweden are building in Johansson’s homeland. He added: “I definitely see the point of that's needed. I mean, Denmark, they've been working also now for some years.

“They have a blueprint now in place for how to build that centre, Sweden the same. Uh, we know that other countries, they did it 20 years ago, like like the Belgians and the Portuguese FA, they did it. They built a latest facility after the Euros. So, of course, it's there to push things and it's needed.”.

Brighton should have right-back Joao Costinha available for Thursday's Uefa Conference League clash despite his late dismissal against Hull City.

The Portuguese defender was sent off in the 89th minute of Sunday's 2-0 Premier League defeat at the MKM Stadium after receiving a second yellow card for his foul on Sorba Thomas.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The dismissal proved costly for Fabian Hurzeler's second placed side, who conceded twice in stoppage time through Oli McBurnie.

However, Costinha will escape a European suspension because his red card was received in a domestic competition.

Under FA rules, receiving a second caution in the same match carries an automatic one-game suspension, which only kicks in for the domestic league and domestic cups.

That means Costinha will miss this Sunday’s match Premier League clash against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium but should be available for Albion’s trip to Bournemouth on December 2.

Uefa operates separately to the Premier League which means Costinha can feature against Universitatea Craiova at the Amex Stadium on Thursday.

Hurzeler admitted the sending-off had a significant impact on Brighton's defeat but insisted the referee was not responsible for the result.

"Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role," he stated.

The German added: "For 65 minutes we demonstrated a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards.

It has been revealed that "In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going.".

Hurzeler also refused to blame referee Peter Bankes, saying: "The referee wasn't the reason why we lost.".

  • Former Sporting midfielder Manuel Ugarte (knee), Carlos Baleba (hamstring) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Luke Shaw (muscle), Marcus Rashford (hip) and Karl Darlow (knee) are all doubtful and will need assessing ahead of kickoff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 14:45, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:11.

Mauricio Pochettino could be without as many as seven Manchester United players for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Former Sporting midfielder Manuel Ugarte (knee), Carlos Baleba (hamstring) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Luke Shaw (muscle), Marcus Rashford (hip) and Karl Darlow (knee) are all doubtful and will need assessing ahead of kickoff.

Matheus Cunha scored two late goals in Man United’s 3-2 comeback victory over Roma on matchday four, but he was then sent off for two bookable offences and will now serve a one-match suspension on Wednesday.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, is available to return to the UCL squad after serving his own one-game ban following a red card against Atletico Madrid last month – he also received a straight red card in Man United’s heavy 4-0 Premier League defeat to Liverpool on Sunday, but will instead serve a domestic ban for that dismissal.

Yoro could therefore continue as a centre-back against Sporting, with Pochettino to weigh up whether to stick with a back three/five system with wing-backs or revert to a four-man defence.

Matthijs de Ligt was handed his first PL start in 357 games by Pochettino after recovering from a long-term injury, but the Dutchman endured a difficult return to the Red Devils side and may be pulled out of the starting lineup in midweek.

Harry Maguire would be the most likely name to replace De Ligt and could start as one of three central defenders next to Yoro and Lisandro Martinez, with Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu operating as wing-backs.

Noussair Mazraoui is an alternative who could start as a right or left-sided full-back in a back four, or as a wing-back, with Dalot potentially operating on the opposite side, allowing Dorgu to push further forward and play in an attacking role.

Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and captain Bruno Fernandes are expected to continue in their central midfield roles, the latter is set to face his former club for the first time since leaving to join Man United in January 2020.

Bryan Mbeumo could retain his starting spot as a centre-forward, but Pochettino may be tempted to hand Joshua Zirkzee a rare start up front, with Mbeumo moving over to the right side of attack. However, Amad Diallo could instead play on the right which would likely keep Mbeumo through the middle.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:.

Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Dalot, Mainoo, Tielemans, Dorgu; Mbeumo, Fernandes; Zirkzee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic’s historic European dream hinges on remaining unbeaten in their next two Europa League ties in Portugal and Cyprus as they seek to build on the win over Besiktas before the international break.

According to recent reports, this, at least, is manager Martin O'Neill's view ahead of Thursday night's clash against Torreense, who have already amassed twice as many points as Celtic. The Portuguese second-tier side might be the most likely source of the win O'Neill feels is required. He has challenged his team to secure four points from the next two away fixtures.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

According to recent reports, the 3-2 win over Besiktas earlier this month breathed some life back into the Parkhead club’s European campaign. "It gives us a chance, you know," remarked O'Neill.

Celtic are currently sitting 32nd out of 36 teams in the standings. They will have to break new ground to finish among the top 24 and secure a place in the knockout stage. No team has managed to do so after opening with three defeats in the new European league format.

Recent findings suggest that after Torreense in Leiria on Thursday Celtic travel to meet Omonia Nicosia in their final European game before Christmas. They play Marseille and Union St. Gilloise early in the upcoming year.

In a recent development, “You'd have to think that we'd need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance so that you've got two left over, including a home game, which will not be easy," mentioned O'Neill. "It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

In a recent development, "We've taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so," he added. "It's the aim of the football club, it's what we've always remarked." O’Neill recalled a sponsors’ event last week where someone mentioned the manner of the Champions League qualifying exit. “Sometimes you feel as if we've never really got over the LASK thing,” he said.

Although much is at stake, O’Neill is still confident that bit-part players to date such as Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg can play a part in the European effort.

In a recent development, both were signed on the last day of the summer transfer window and were included in the European squad. Sorensen has failed to make an impression despite starting the opening two Europa League defeats against Ferencvaros and Benfica while Van den Berg has been sidelined with an ankle injury.

The Dutch midfielder made his belated debut as a substitute in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Sorensen, meanwhile, has not featured in the last two matchday squads due to a family bereavement. Celtic face a period where auxiliary players will be required to step up.

Industry observers note that “This is a chance, with a bit of luck, for the likes of Sorensen and Van den Berg,” said O’Neill. He challenged Van den Berg to kick on following his cameo at the weekend. He hopes Sorensen, too, can begin to nail down a regular place in the side.

"He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,” noted the manager “I think that he also arrived late as well too, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do.

"And whatever we do, I bet you it'll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma. But now it would be up to him.”.

Recent findings suggest that viljami Sinisalo has been waiting for his turn back in goal. O’Neill still hasn't made up mind about who will stay at No. 1.

Sam Johnstone is clearly in possession of the gloves at present even if it would not be a surprise if Sinisalo is given a match before long, perhaps as soon as Thursday. “There’s still good competition,” remarked the manager. “Viljami wants to be the keeper here, which is great.

“He will play again and at some stage you have to make you’re mind up who will stay as no.1. I don’t think there’s a phenomenal amount between them at this stage.”.

The Seagulls are second in the Premier League table despite last Sunday’s painful 2-0 loss at Hull City. This Thursday they welcome Romanian League leaders Craiova for a Uefa Conference League clash and on Sunday they return to Premier League action as Newcastle visit the Amex.

Here is the latest injury news, including Hurzeler's comments and potential return dates.

Mitoma remains one of Brighton's biggest injury concerns. The Japan international has been sidelined with a lengthy hamstring problem and is yet to feature this season.

Hurzeler told Sussex World last week that the winger is getting closer to a comeback and indicated that Mitoma was around one or two weeks away.

The Nottingham Forest fixture on December 5 could be a potential return date.

Tzimas is recovering from a serious knee injury, having suffered an ACL problem which has kept him out for an extended period.

The Greek striker has returned to training with the first team, but Hurzeler has stressed that patience is required.

"Stefanos is a special character," he stated, praising the forward's determination during his rehabilitation.

The manager added that Tzimas would not immediately be an option, despite being pleased with his progress.

There is chance that he could return at Bournemouth on December 2 but Brighton will not take any chances.

Ferguson continues his recovery from an ankle/foot injury and remains a long-term absentee.

Hurzeler previously explained that Ferguson's recovery was similar to Tzimas's situation, saying: "We have to wait some more weeks.".

December seems increasingly unlikely for Ferguson with January perhaps a more realistic option.

In a recent development, yalcouye is the latest player to suffer an injury setback. The midfielder picked up a problem after returning from international duty with the Ivory Coast, where he featured in two matches.

In a recent development, hurzeler confirmed on November 22 that the youngster would be unavailable for several weeks. "Malick had a bigger matter coming back from the Ivory Coast with an injury and therefore we have to expect that he is a few weeks out," he remarked.

Brighton vs Everton on December 13 is a potential return date.

Yohanna has suffered a frustrating setback after picking up another thigh injury while representing Nigeria's Under-23 side.

The winger had been working towards a return following an earlier muscle problem but suffered a recurrence during international duty.

Hurzeler remarked: "Unfortunately, he got a re-injury when he was with Nigeria. Unfortunately, it wasn't perfectly managed.".

He added that Brighton would support the youngster through what he described as a tough period.

There is currently no confirmed return date.

Hadjam is another recent addition to the injury list after picking up a knee problem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Raith Rovers have been charged by the Scottish Football Association over a social media post mocking Dunfermline Athletic manager Neil Lennon in the aftermath of the Fife derby.

Following the 0-0 draw at Stark's Park on November 6, Lennon made a pinching gesture with his thumb and forefinger towards rival supporters which was widely interpreted as a jibe calling Raith Rovers a "small club".

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Shortly after the final whistle, Raith's official X account shared a photo of Lennon making the gesture alongside the caption, "How big is your penis, Neil?". The club deleted the post 52 minutes later after it went viral.

The SFA compliance officer has now issued the Kirkcaldy outfit with a notice of complaint relating to a breach of Disciplinary Rule 73, which reads: "No recognised football body, club, official, Team Official or other member of Team Staff, player, match official or other person under the jurisdiction of the Scottish FA shall in an interview, a ‘blog’ on the internet, on a social networking or micro-blogging site, or in any other manner calculated or likely to lead to publicity, make comment(s) of a discriminatory or offensive nature based on, but not limited to, race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation or disability, or that endorse or encourage foul play or violent Conduct or are otherwise offensive.

"There shall be a presumption that any material published in such a manner was published in the name of and/or with the authority of the person or body bearing to have published the material.".

Sanctions typically start at a £500 lower-end fine and rise up to a £5,000 top-end fine.

Speaking about the incident last week, Lennon described the episode as "embarrassing for them", referring to Raith, adding; "“You know, that’s like an official club Twitter account, which is embarrassing. I’ll say no more than that.”.

According to recent reports, raith are scheduled to face a Hampden disciplinary hearing on December 17. This falls just over a week before the two sides meet again at East End Park on Boxing Day.

Latest Update: Macdonald: I was told my job was ‘bomb-proof’ – but eight days later Eastbourne Town sacked me

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1154 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Macdonald’s four-and-a-half year run as manager of Town ended after Saturday’s 1-1 draw at home to Whitstable when he was sacked in a move that has angered many of the club’s fans and seen a number of players and support staff leave the club too.
  • He has spoken to Sussexworld and the Eastbourne Herald about the decision – and outlined some of the difficulties they had faced with injury and unavailability this season in a run of results that ironically had recently looked like it might be coming to an end.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Macdonald’s four-and-a-half year run as manager of Town ended after Saturday’s 1-1 draw at home to Whitstable when he was sacked in a move that has angered many of the club’s fans and seen a number of players and support staff leave the club too.

He has spoken to Sussexworld and the Eastbourne Herald about the decision – and outlined some of the difficulties they had faced with injury and unavailability this season in a run of results that ironically had recently looked like it might be coming to an end.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Town confirmed Macdonald’s departure on Saturday in a statement and have since installed club stalwart Dave Winterton as interim manager and asked fans to get behind him.

Macdonald said of his sacking: “It was a surprise to be honest and there was absolutely zero warning, which you often anticipate with this sort of thing.

"I spoke to the chairman eight days earlier (the day before the Sheppey game) and he told me on that call that my role was “bomb-proof” and that I had his backing.

"I had explained to him in the call how hard it had been this season, but we didn’t have a relationship where we talked regularly on the phone so we hadn’t had an opportunity to discuss things previously.

Recent findings suggest that "On Saturday, the chairman told one of my assistants at the final whistle to tell me to come to the office. It was the first league game that the chairman had attended since August so I obviously didn’t think too much of it, but that was when he delivered the news to me around 20 minutes after the game had finished.

"He did it along with another member of staff who I’ve never been introduced to before, but is also apparently a committee member.

"The chairman told me my position was being ended at the club and stated that they thought it would be better to announce it as a resignation, which I rejected.

"I wasn’t given a reason, despite asking for one multiple times. The chairman just kept shrugging and it wasn’t his fault it was just what the board wanted. I was told that the board held a vote on the previous Monday (November 16) and the decision was made, which is when they made a call to another manager on speaker to offer the job/sound out his interest. The likely newly introduced manager told me this on Saturday evening.

"The club then let me manage the Lewes game on the Tuesday, take training Thursday, sign two players on Friday and manage Saturday’s game without anybody saying anything to me, despite knowing they were going to sack me after the Saturday game.".

It has been revealed that it is Macdonald and one of his right-hand men, Ben Davis, who have been sacked. Macdonald stated: “The club wanted my other two assistants, Matthew Elphick and Adam Davidson, to remain in position, but they have rejected that opportunity.”.

Macdonald outlined some of the difficulties Town have faced this season which have left them struggling, having won just two league games to sit second from bottom of the Isthmian SE table after 19 games.

He told us: “It has been no secret that we have been completely decimated by injuries through the season and have only once played the same XI two games running. We had started to get bodies in the door and back on the pitch.

"We’d drawn our last two games and arguably could have won both, so it is frustrating that the club made the call they did when the tide was clearly turning.”.

Macdonald outlined the injuries the squad had faced: Oliver Davies - ruptured PCL; Anesu Sismayi - Head injury; Marcin Ruda - fractured foot; JJ Walker - hip flexor & suspension; Leon Greig - knee injury (3 months missed); Luke Emberson - shin splints & groin; Aussie Pugh - ankle & knee; Aaron Capon - hamstring & back; Jack Murphy - heel & suspension; Sonny Walsh - jaw; Eliot Jenks - hamstring; Oli Deda - concussion (missed 3 games); Reuel Powell-Downey - hamstring; Arron Hopkinson - suspension.

He added: “That is a fraction of the list.”.

Recent findings suggest that looking back at his time as Town boss, Macdonald talked about some of those who had helped him and his staff: “Since we’ve been at the club, David Jenkins has been absolutely incredible. The work he does for the club, the selflessness and support he gives it is truly unbelievable. He is what non-league is about. Anything we needed, he always did his best to help us with.

"Ross Perrin this season has also been a huge help to us and supported us throughout, as have Luci Del-Gaudio and Paul Lewis. Josh Claxton and Ed have both been incredible. What Josh has done with the social media and all other online stuff is just amazing and he done so much for the club that never got noticed. Josh has also left the football club.

"Former 23s and 18s managers Shaun Lee, Giuseppe Lombardelli and Ryan Reid were always a huge help and incredibly supportive. There are dozens of others that have backed and supported us throughout our time like Ken Wilkins and Chris Prior. Truly great people.

"A huge thank you to all the players over the years. They have done so much for us and we really appreciate all their efforts.

"The biggest thank you is to our management team and support staff, who have just been incredible throughout our time together at the club. Ben Davis, Matt Elphick, Adam Davidson, David Winterton, Roman Glazier and Dom Crowhurst have all made my Saturdays so enjoyable. They’ve all worked so hard for the players and deserve huge credit.”.

Macdonald is in no hurry to find a newly introduced non-league job: “I would expect to relax and have a break from it all to be honest. I will try to take in other games and training sessions with other managers wherever I can. I’m trying not to think too much about what comes next because you can’t predict anything in non-league.”.

He added: “You don’t often get the chance to manage the club from the town you grew up in and I’ve just committed over 10% of my life to it, so the next few days and weeks will just be reflecting on that and appreciating the opportunity that the club gave me four-and-a-half years ago, and the continued and consistent success we have given them in return.”.

We asked Eastbourne Town if anyone wished to respond to any of Macdonald’s comments and a statement from the committee said: “The club will make further statements in due course, no further comments at this time.”.

There are evenings when tactical blueprints dissolve into sheer, unscripted theatre, and for 45 minutes at a rain-soaked Ibrox, it appeared as though Derek McInnes’ best-laid plans had conspired against his own side. Yet by the time a frenetic second half had run its course, Rangers had conjured an epic turnaround to claim a breathless 3–2 victory over Aberdeen that saw them move within a point of idle Premiership leaders Celtic.

In testing conditions, both sides abandoned any pretence of caution to serve up a thrilling second half that was in stark contrast to the opening 45 minutes, which offered little beyond frustration and creeping anxiety for the Rangers manager.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Facing the club where he spent eight formative years in the dugout, McInnes had tinkered with his starting formation, handing Ben Godfrey a first start since July 31st as part of a three-man defence designed to counter their opponents narrow, winger-less system, However, the hosts looked entirely disjointed.

Rangers, playing their first home match in a full month following an unusual sequence of five consecutive away fixtures, began on the front foot. However, despite Dan Neil squandering a glorious opportunity from six yards inside the opening 60 seconds, his rebound subsequently struck off teammate Ryan Naderi, the home side struggled to establish rhythm or coherence.

It has been revealed that aberdeen, aiming to build on their first win under fresh head coach Mario Frick at the weekend, sensed vulnerability and grew steadily in conviction. Organised in a compact 4-3-1-2 shape, the visitors frustrated Rangers before delivering a clinical blow on the half-hour mark. Brad Lyons capitalised on Rangers’ hesitation from a corner to produce a diving header that was hooked off the line by Nico Raskin. However, after VAR intervened, the ball was adjudged to have crossed the line and referee John Beaton awarded the goal, sparking wild celebrations scenes in the away end.

It has been revealed that worse almost followed for the hosts. Only profligacy in front of goal, most notably from Moroccan striker Ayoub Mouloua, who twice spurned clear openings before the interval, prevented the Dons from carrying a more commanding lead into the break as the Rangers supporters made their dissatisfaction known.

It has been revealed that if the first half belonged to Aberdeen’s disciplined industry, the opening 12 minutes of the second belonged to Rangers’ ruthless efficiency. McInnes wasted little time in rectifying his questionable team selection, executing a bold triple substitution at half-time that saw Kim Min-su, Tuur Rommens and Findlay Curtis replace Kevin Kelsy, Godfrey, and Badredine Bouanani.

Industry observers note that the transformation was instantaneous. Within 60 seconds of the restart, Min-su tested Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Müller with a dipping shot. Müller could only parry the ball directly into the path of Ryan Naderi, who gleefully dispatched the rebound from close range to restore parity.

Recent findings suggest that before Aberdeen could draw breath, Ibrox erupted once more. Just 64 seconds after the equaliser, Naderi turned provider, threading an incisive pass into Djeidi Gassama. Outpacing his man, the winger kept his composure to drill a low finish across Müller into the far corner. In barely a minute, a packed stadium that had been growing increasingly restless was suddenly alive again.

Rangers’ third arrived in the 56th minute via a devastating counter-attack. Min-su, whose introduction had injected vital urgency into the hosts' attacking play, won possession deep inside his own half and drove up field before releasing Gassama. Cutting the ball neatly across the penalty area, the Mauritanian international teed up Raskin, who coolly side-footed low across Müller to establish a seemingly decisive 3-1 advantage.

Aberdeen, however, refused to crumble. Barely a minute after Raskin’s goal, Alexander Briedl drifted inside from the left flank and slipped a weighted pass into the path of Findlay Marshall. The youngster met it cleanly, sending a crisp drive crashing in off the post to reduce the deficit and reignite a pulsating contest.

Recent findings suggest that what followed was a nerve-shredding final half-hour punctuated by transitions and agonising near-misses. Aberdeen’s Nesta Guinness-Walker endured frustration when his late penalty appeal was waved away. In between, Marshall came within inches of securing a share of the spoils, dragging a left-footed effort agonisingly wide of Pandur's post in the closing stages after the Croatian had made a spectacular save to deny Nicky Devlin from a corner at his front post.

If Scottish football occasionally stands accused of predictability, nobody among the 50,738 crowd could reasonably complain of short measure. Rangers survived, although not without making their supporters endure another uncomfortable finale as they took advantage of their game in hand to move closer to keeper their title challenge firmly on track.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eight goals were shared in a crazy 4-4 contest that lurched in all directions, the Isthmian Premier points shared, a proper sporting contest in the best traditions of non-league football.

Old men have long memories. Well before kick-off, sitting up in Enfield's distinctive Art Deco grandstand, I fell into conversation with an octogenarian - 83 to be exact, as he proudly told me - who had travelled up to this fixture from his Littlehampton home. But he was born and raised in North London, and he proudly recounted his Wembley trips for FA Amateur Cup finals with the old Enfield FC.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Ah yes, chipped in your Herald reporter, 1966 against Skelmersdale - I too was there, on a Wembley day out with my own football-daft dad! And if that anecdote is worth a column inch, it is because non-league football ripples with such memories.

Recent findings suggest that down below us, the teams had done their warm-up routines, taken in all the instructions, and - to a guard of honour from the local primary school - were filing out for a crucial Isthmian Premier contest. Second versus third; valuable points to play for.

It has been revealed that borough flew out of the traps, and after a couple of Freddie Carter long throws had ruffled the home defence, they were ahead on seven minutes. Terrell Egbri, a turbo-charged winger all afternoon, cut in from the right to whip in a cross - or was it a shot? Either way, the ball spun wickedly in off the woodwork past helpless home keeper Thompson.

Both sides were energised, and play swung end to end with a glorious lack of caution and Thomas Avgoustidis levelled for Town.

The Sports looked stronger, swarming all over the home defence, and Liam Nash flicked a back-header just over, then the industrious Max Sheaf combined with Nash for a fizzing low ball across the Enflied goalmouth - but nobody managed a touch.

Steve King's side were not to be denied. Sam Oguntayo - nominally a full-back but so often a marauding extra attacker - swung over a cross which Thompson pushed over for a Borough corner, recycled and whacked goalwards by Sheaf. With Enfield throwing bodies into the mix, the unfortunate Tommy Avgoustidis back-headed into his own net for a 2-1 Borough lead.

Industry observers note that it is axiomatic among coaches that you need to score when your side is on top - even with a lead. When King and his staff looked back on the 15 minutes to half-time, they will have noted five or six chances to have put this game to bed – though credit goes to home keeper Thompson for some alert stops and one brilliant save to deny Darren McQueen.

Recent findings suggest that but the start of the second half saw a huge momentum swing: Enfield introduced Orient loanee Tariq Al Sadee - fresh from international action with Oman - and the home side had reclaimed the midfield initiative. An excellent Lewis Carey save denied Avgoustidis and then Oguntayo cleared off the line from one of four home corners.

And just as King was reinforcing his midfield with Craig Eastmond off the bench, the Towners seized an equaliser, Luke May-Parrott streaking away to beat Carey. 2-2, and half-hour of mayhem, magic and madness to come.

Sources indicate that for a while, Borough were reeling. Tariq was striding everywhere and Enfield were revitalised. On 63 minutes, a pass through the right flank sliced open the Sports, and Luke May-Parrott's low angled shot put the home side ahead for the first time.

McQueen almost restored parity but put his shot just wide. And with the Sports pressing high and possibly a tiny bit overstretched, a long clearance out of the Enfield defence allowed Avgoustidis to pound through open space and strike an effort which Carey should really have stopped, but it squirmed over the line for 4-2.

At this point routine, sensible football matches peter out, as winning sides shut down, losing sides struggle for openings and chances, everything goes to script, and everybody consigns the result to history. Fortunately, King prefers his teams to write their own scripts. With Kai Corbett and Tyano Wilson bringing fresh impetus off the bench, Borough were energised again.

Wilson was getting possession in dangerous areas, and he squirmed in from the left to drill a lethal low ball across the goalmouth. Corbett pounced from close range, and the match was alive again at 4-3.

Recent findings suggest that and with the Towners showing no real signs, or capacity, to shut down the match, we had a brilliant climax to relish. The Sports were chasing down everything, and Enfield were flapping.

In a recent development, that final goal just had to be Borough's. With seven minutes to play, Kai Corbett was released from halfway to tear into the Enfield defence. Cutting in from the right, he chose to shoot early and rocketed his low shot into the right hand corner of the home net.

Industry observers note that eight goals shared, the points shared, and an engrossing, exhausting non-league football match shared. Football should always be like this.

You can pay much, much more for a seat in a splendid Premier League stadium - albeit segregated and strictly policed - and you might even see an eight-goal thriller. But up in Enfield Town's quirky main stand, as spectators shook hands all around, one home supporter summed it up perfectly: "Thank goodness neither side lost!".

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34.

Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.

Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.

Although missing out on European football came as a major blow to Rangers at the time, it has enabled Derek McInnes's side to build up a head of steam on the domestic front.

Rangers have put together a 13-match unbeaten streak since that exit to Jablonec in the Conference League playoff round, recording 11 wins and two draws.

While being held to a 2-2 draw at Hearts before the November international break frustrated McInnes, Rangers have responded with a victory over Aberdeen in the League Cup and successive top-flight triumphs.

A 2-0 success at St Mirren was followed by an hard-earned 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday, Rangers sealing the three points through an 88th-minute own goal.

Eight of Rangers' 13 league matches have been played away from Ibrox, giving them a chance to make the most of competing on home territory, with seven goals being scored in their last two such games in the Scottish Premiership.

Over the international break, Liechtenstein legend Mario Frick was named as the fresh Aberdeen head coach.

The surprise development was followed by Frick delivering a 4-2 victory at Kilmarnock in his first game in charge.

A much-needed win has led to the Dons moving into eighth spot, albeit still just three points above the relegation zone.

With Aberdeen having lost five of the six matches preceding his arrival, Frick will not be getting carried away with three points versus bottom-of-the-table opposition.

Nevertheless, Aberdeen have now accumulated seven points from their most recent four away games in the Scottish Premiership, something which cannot be ignored by their hosts.

Aberdeen Scottish Premiership form:.

If McInnes makes any changes to his Rangers XI, Findlay Curtis and Kevin Kelsy are favourites to be introduced in the final third.

Recent findings suggest that while Cameron Devlin is making progress in his recovery from injury, this game is expected to come too soon for the midfielder. The same applies to Lawrence Shankland, who has recently returned to light training after a significant hamstring injury.

Ryan Naderi has contributed either a goal or assist in eight of his last nine Scottish Premiership appearances.

Afeez Aremu, Findlay Marshall and Ayoub Mouloua are all options to return for Aberdeen after they made an impact from the substitutes' bench at Kilmarnock.

Connor Ronan remains an injury doubt after missing that fixture, while this match comes too soon for defender Mats Knoester. Chris Cadden is pushing for a return to the squad after a hamstring issue.

Rangers possible starting lineup:.

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Rommens; Neil, Raskin; Bouanani, Naderi, Findlay; Kelsy.

Aberdeen possible starting lineup:.

Muller; Devlin, Milne, Molloy, Guinness-Walker; Lyons, Aremu, Briedl; Marshall; Mouloua, Nisbet.

Sources indicate that with Aberdeen having made a positive start to life under Frick, they will back themselves to earn a result at Ibrox. However, given the chance to move within a point of Celtic, we feel that Rangers will do just enough to secure three points in a competitive fixture.

Hibs head coach Marink Reedijk was delighted with his team’s display as they overcame Dundee 2-1 to claim a first home league win in nearly eight months.

The Leith side struck twice in the space of three minutes just before half-time with Martin Boyle converting from the penalty spot and Nicky Cadden producing a stunning finish.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Dundee – hurting from Saturday’s 8-0 hammering by Hearts – put up a fight after the interval and Joe Wright’s strike gave them hope of a comeback.

But Hibs held on to secure their first league victory in front of their own supporters since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Reedijk said: “It’s always nice to win, it’s a good one again in order to make sure we get confirmation that if we show our identity about intensity, aggression and proactivity and are brave, that anything can happen here.

“I hope we get another three points next match and that we go again in a way that we do the things we are good at and what our identity and what we stand for is.

“The next match against Motherwell is not at home, I know, but there will be a match at home against Rangers, where this can also come to life again. But that is far away.

“First things first, Saturday lies another challenge.”.

Reedijk was also pleased to see Cadden rack up a stunning strike – the wing-back finding the net in only his second start of the season.

The effort came from a cleverly worked corner routine, with Hibs having already threatened from a similar set-piece earlier in the match.

Reedijk also singled out assistant coach Rogier Molhoek for praise for devising the short corner routines.

He added: “It was a beautiful goal, wasn’t it? It was one when he left the foot, I was like, ‘ooh, he hits it well and you saw the angle of the ball’.

According to recent reports, “We try to use every quality we have in order to make it difficult for opponents to see what we are doing in the beginning. Also we look at their organisation and if their organisation allows us to attack certain spaces, we try to do this.

“This is the job of Rogier, he always makes routines – and also with crazy names. You will never know these names because sometimes it’s not polite.”.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley was encouraged by his side’s response to the humiliation against Hearts despite his team falling to a third consecutive league loss.

Recent findings suggest that he remarked: “Both teams are a bit fragile and there was a lot of trepidation in the game but the one thing about us we got a degree of pride back. It’s not the result but a little bit of stability and we revealed a lot of courage.

“We wanted to give ourselves a foundation to build from and we gave ourselves that.

“We were much more cohesive in the second half and when you suffer the defeat we suffered on Saturday and you come here and you find yourself 2-0 down at half-time, it asks a lot of questions of you as a group and I thought they responded brilliantly.

“They showed courage and spirit and it’s not been easy because there’s a fragility about us. We responded in the proper manner.”.

Crawley’s box was under a lot of pressure in the second half. However, it was the Reds who had the first effort of the half. Dylan Morgan got hold of a half clearance, laid it off to Lewis Richards, who fired a shot goalward, but it was well saved by Cox for a corner.

Recent findings suggest that it was then the Bees who had the better chances. Firstly, Kellan Gordon gave away a free kick on the edge of the box by Zac Williams, which bobbles around the box and eventually finds a way past the post with Mannone beaten.

Industry observers note that A few minutes later, Idris Kanu had a shot parried by Mannone, but only to Charlie Lakin, who hit the bar and then dribbled a shot past the post. Mannone was having a great game, and he was called into action again when Crichlow-Noble latched onto a free kick from just outside the box, and Mannone parried away through a crowd of players.

Sources indicate that lakin had another shot from just inside the box but saved by Mannone from a tight angle. Adam Senior also had a great chance, as his header down bounced back to him and he fired over the bar from close range.

The game finally settled down in the final 20 minutes, and Crawley managed to see the game out for a valuable point, which sees the Reds level on points with Rotherham in 23rd, with a game in hand.

Crawley’s next game is away to Exeter City for a 12:30pm kick off this Saturday, and then at home to Port Vale the following Tuesday (1st Dec).

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 13:39 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:49 EST, 22 November 2026.

Yang Hyun-jun is predicting that Celtic can make Europa League history by bouncing back from a dismal start in the group stage to qualify.

Since the competition was revamped by UEFA in 2024, no side have made it through to the knock-out round having lost their first three games.

With defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo arriving in quick succession, Martin O’Neill’s men looked to be heading for an early exit.

After beating Besiktas last time out, however, they are still in with a shout when matchday five takes them to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday.

Winger Yang, who made his first start since early September in the win over St Mirren on Saturday, feels there’s a growing belief among the players they can yet emulate last season’s feat of reaching the play-off round.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Can we make history? Of course,’ he noted. ‘We believe we can qualify. We are getting better all the time. You could see that against Besiktas.

Yang made his first start since early September in Celtic's victory over St Mirren on Saturday.

Martin O'Neill aims to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive by beating Torreense this week.

‘They are a very good team, and that has given us the belief that we can go to the next round. It’s important to take it game-by-game, though. This is the most important one. If we can get the points we can go on from there, step-by-step.’.

Torreense made history last season by becoming the first second-tier team to win the Portuguese Cup and qualify for Europe. Despite currently sitting 13th in that division, they have confounded expectations by taking six points from four Europa League games.

In a recent development, ‘We are playing against a Portuguese second division team but we have to be focused and aggressive,’ warned Yang. ‘They are higher than us in the Europa League table. They’ve already won two matches so they will be a good team.

‘We have to approach it the same way as we would playing a team like Benfica or Sporting Lisbon. We have to go there and try to win. If we play like we did against St Mirren, we can do it.’.

Meanwhile, Yang is adamant that being made exempt from military service wasn’t even on his mind as South Korea won the Asian Games this year.

Played in Japan in September and October, Yang’s side defeated the hosts 1-0 in the final.

That meant all the South Korean players were no longer obliged to spend time serving in the military before they turn 28.

According to recent reports, yang, 24, who suffered a hamstring injury in the opening victory against Qatar, reflected: ‘It was great. Obviously, it was nice to win it but I also got injured, which was unfortunate.

‘I was trying to be around the team, to help in any way I could.

‘It wasn’t really about the national service. Everyone was playing for the team, the country and the fans.

Industry observers note that ‘We managed to get the victory. Being exempt from national service was just a bonus, I guess.

According to recent reports, ‘The celebrations were enjoyable. It’s the first time my national team have won the Asian Games.

It has been revealed that ‘It was really hard — especially the game against Japan. It was a great achievement.’.
